frontend.reason: The Helm surface searches registered sources without a hardcoded chart list and preserves query, source, provider, all-version, chart, and version identity in validated URL state.

backend.reason: Exact source, chart, and version detail remains read-only unless it matches an existing server-owned digest-pinned OCI recipe; available installation reuses the current Agent command and durable OperationEvent contract.

frontend.reason: Strict chart detail, values-schema availability, and recipe-gated installation share the existing confirmation dialog, typed target, command receipt, and operation-status stream.

backend.reason: Fixed-host bounded transport projects only typed chart and trust metadata.

frontend.reason: Bounded search renders typed trust badges without promoting discovery to execution.

backend.reason: Latest and exact-version details are escaped and bounded without creating an executable mapping.

frontend.reason: Exact read-only discovery details expose no external install action.

backend.reason: The digest-pinned server recipe now returns the common staged CommandReceipt, preserves catalog idempotency, and emits the first durable OperationEvent before Agent execution.

frontend.reason: The wizard consumes server-owned targets and hands the accepted command to the shared operation dock.

realtime.reason: Accepted catalog commands can reuse the single durable, resumable OperationEvent stream without a Helm-specific progress protocol.

backend.reason: The dedicated Python endpoint pins an observed release revision, enforces DEPLOY_RUN and the live agent capability, accepts only a digest-pinned server recipe, validates typed values server-side, and returns the common audited CommandReceipt before the existing atomic Helm executor runs.

frontend.reason: The detail page exposes Upgrade only from a server-advertised capability, renders the server-owned typed value inputs, confirms target and diff once, submits no raw chart or repository input, and hands the receipt to the shared operation dock.

realtime.reason: Upgrade acceptance stages the first durable OperationEvent in the command transaction and the existing resumable stream carries progress, cancellation, failure, and completion for the exact command ID.

backend.reason: Server and Agent double-revalidate exact release CAS evidence before bounded rollback.

frontend.reason: Only older observed revisions can be confirmed and sent to the shared operation dock.

realtime.reason: The audited receipt starts the shared resumable rollback operation stream.

backend.reason: The target Agent renders a digest-pinned revision-bound candidate and returns only a bounded redacted resource diff.

frontend.reason: The values editor strictly validates and renders the shared redacted resource diff while preserving the existing upgrade flow when preview is unavailable.

backend.reason: Values apply reuses the reviewed revision-bound upgrade, Agent CAS, audit, and stream.

frontend.reason: One shared typed values editor validates declared inputs and confirms the exact target diff.

backend.reason: Exact release CAS evidence is double-revalidated before bounded uninstall.

frontend.reason: The destructive action is capability-gated and exact-target confirmed before dispatch.

backend.reason: One authorized bounded aggregate preserves registered bindings and projects observed Argo and Flux controller/source identities, status, health, labels, freshness, capability evidence, and partial reasons without raw CR payloads or per-row reads.

frontend.reason: The fleet table consumes the canonical mixed overview in one request, preserves registered rows, shows observed controller evidence and partial coverage, and links exact resources to the shared GitOps detail route without browser CR normalization.

backend.reason: One bounded inventory batch projects exact owns, source, and depends_on edges with explicit partial-coverage reasons and no per-node queries.

frontend.reason: The repository-owned compact workspace renders the observed controller tree, coverage state, exact selectable resource identities, and prevents the root resource from opening a recursive detail portal.

backend.reason: Observed controller status, health, revision, source, conditions, bounded history, and revision-bound capabilities are projected without manufacturing provider state.

frontend.reason: The compact repository workspace renders typed controller insights and history while exposing only server-advertised actions.

backend.reason: Reconcile is RBAC- and capability-gated, CAS-bound to an exact ResourceRef, and returns the canonical CommandReceipt with OperationEvent streaming.

frontend.reason: The shared confirmation flow dispatches reconcile only when present in the current CapabilitySet and follows the existing operation stream.

backend.reason: Sync-with-source carries exact root and source UIDs and resourceVersions, revalidates both live resources, then reconciles source before root.

frontend.reason: Sync-with-source uses the same typed confirmation and receipt flow without conflating product release commands with provider control.

backend.reason: Flux spec suspension and evidence-preserving Argo auto-sync suspension/resume are exact-resource CAS operations behind the shared audit flow.

frontend.reason: Suspend or resume is shown from the latest controller CapabilitySet and uses the common impact-confirmation dialog.

backend.reason: Argo sync supports revision, prune, dry-run, force, apply-only, provider options, and selective resources with both inventory ownership and live controller ownership checks.

frontend.reason: Typed sync controls submit exact selected tree identities and an idempotency key through the shared CommandReceipt contract.

backend.reason: Normal and hard Argo refresh are distinct audited controller annotations, revision-bound and dispatched through the command event path.

frontend.reason: Browser refetch remains separate while the refresh action dialog explicitly selects normal or hard provider refresh.

backend.reason: The product-owned rollback acts on the exact authorized release run and application steps with policy checks, persisted state, and audit evidence.

frontend.reason: GitOps run controls reuse the canonical rollback action rather than adding a provider-specific adapter.

backend.reason: Cancellation is RBAC checked, transition validated, persisted, and audit recorded for the product release run.

frontend.reason: The existing terminate user intent maps to the canonical cancel transition at the product workflow boundary.

backend.reason: Pause and resume are state-validated, workspace-scoped, persisted release-run transitions with audit events.

frontend.reason: The GitOps workspace already consumes the shared pause and resume action union.

backend.reason: The server compiles fixed OpenCost allocation queries into the outbound cluster-agent evidence policy, persists results in evidence windows, and reads one workspace/cluster/time/rank-bounded batch containing only the namespace hourly and storage JSON fragments required to project integer micro-unit summary values without a direct Prometheus connection.

frontend.reason: The Cost route validates observed/partial/unavailable unions, preserves server-computed micro-units, formats the observed currency, and keeps missing values distinct from observed zero.

backend.reason: The server compiles fixed pod allocation and use queries into the outbound cluster-agent policy, reads one workspace/cluster/time/rank-bounded evidence batch alongside the authorized workload graph, and projects only graph-selected pod costs in integer micro-units without direct Prometheus access.

frontend.reason: The shared workload Cost tab validates observed, partial, and unavailable contracts, renders server-computed current allocation and bounded history, and never derives currency or rates in the browser.

backend.reason: The trend derives from historical outbound-agent evidence windows rather than a browser or server range query, isolates cluster/namespace identities, retains at most eight series and 480 ordered points, and reports insufficient or truncated evidence explicitly.

The normalized /api/cost/nodes contract resolves authorized cluster and namespace scope, reads one bounded inventory page plus one bulk metrics projection, and returns provider-neutral node identity, capacity, measured usage, pricing provenance, completeness, pagination, and the server-owned 120-second refresh policy without fabricating monetary values.

frontend.reason: The Cost surface consumes the typed node page through the shared adapter, preserves authorized scope and cursor pagination, follows the response-selected refresh policy, and renders observed capacity and usage with explicit unavailable pricing instead of hardcoded costs.

backend.reason: The source contract reads process-local Go runtime arguments such as kubeconfig paths, listener ports, browser launch, MCP, and timeline retention. That runtime is excluded from the Python and outbound-Agent product architecture, so these deployment-owned values are deliberately unavailable to browser reads; user preferences and Agent-managed integrations remain separate typed contracts.

frontend.reason: The Settings route names the unavailable host boundary and exposes no fake process configuration, while independently implemented preference and integration cards consume their own server contracts.

backend.reason: A browser request cannot replace deployment process arguments or mutate host kubeconfig paths in the Python and outbound-Agent architecture. User preferences still use optimistic revision checks and an atomic audit event, and live Agent integrations use their dedicated command receipts.

frontend.reason: No host-config save control or restart promise is exposed. The existing synchronizer persists only validated user preferences and reloads server authority on revision conflict.

backend.reason: The owner-authorized Python integration contract persists encrypted write-only headers, atomically versions policy and audit evidence, streams one superseding probe operation, and replaces the target-agent metrics provider only after a bounded live probe.

frontend.reason: The typed settings adapter exposes configured header names without secret values, preserves omitted secrets only for the same origin, requires re-entry after origin changes, and follows the shared operation event stream for live probe feedback.

backend.reason: Python serves existing purpose-scoped operation, timeline, topology, and dashboard streams. Context progress is normalized onto the authenticated dashboard scope lifecycle rather than recreating the upstream direct Kubernetes broadcaster.

frontend.reason: One scope owner reuses the shared SSE parser and maps connected, reconnecting, deferred-ready, and heartbeat behavior onto OperationEvent progress/completed semantics plus scoped cache invalidation.

realtime.reason: All live surfaces share strict frame parsing, durable replay or typed resync, a 30-second heartbeat, bounded reconnect, obsolete authority abort, and render-coalesced consumers instead of per-feature ad hoc loops.
